headline: High risk of cascading error and capability conflict: ctx can observe Claude Code events while social-auto-upload can act on account/media workflows, creating unsafe default handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events, so it can ingest another agent’s outputs by default; social-auto-upload operates on account/media workflows and could be influenced if its outputs are bridged into ctx. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ctx is configured to read Claude Code event payloads as instructions, injection risk increases.
IF social-auto-upload output is copied into ctx without provenance checks, malicious text can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all ctx-ingested events.
Disable automatic instruction parsing from tool-output text.
Require manual review before forwarding social-auto-upload output.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and provenance filtering in the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media files. However, B has read_filesystem=false and write_filesystem=false, so a direct shared-workspace leak is not evidenced; the main residual risk is indirect leakage through logs or copied outputs.
conditions: IF account data from social-auto-upload is copied into ctx logs, leakage becomes plausible.
IF ctx logs are exported to a third party, sensitive metadata may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep account data out of ctx logs.
Rotate or redact runtime logs before sharing.
Run the agents in separate OS users.
Avoid copying media/account artifacts between agents.
requires-engineering: add redaction rules for account identifiers and tokens.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and use filesystem/MCP surfaces, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress and handles account files. They do not both have unrestricted write access, so the high-severity same-directory write conflict is not supported; still, overlapping mutable resources and networked side effects create a real coordination risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same account or project directory, conflicts become more likely.
IF ctx installs packages while social-auto-upload is running, environment drift may break uploads.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Freeze dependencies before concurrent runs.
Serialize package installation and upload jobs.
Disable shared mutable state in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx explicitly observes Claude Code events, so its outputs can become authoritative context for another agent; social-auto-upload can then act on account/media workflows with network egress. That creates a plausible default cascade where one agent’s unverified output drives the other’s actions, with potentially irreversible external side effects.
conditions: IF ctx output is forwarded into social-auto-upload without verification, cascading errors are likely.
IF social-auto-upload executes uploads based on ctx-generated metadata, mistakes can propagate externally.
mitigations: Require human approval before uploads.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Log and diff all handoff payloads.
Limit social-auto-upload to dry-run mode.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on ctx-to-upload handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media content. The pair can therefore create retention and subject-rights mismatches if account artifacts are logged or retained differently. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the issue is compliance-process drift rather than a specific legal breach.
conditions: IF account data is written into ctx audit/runtime logs, retention obligations may diverge.
IF deletion requests are applied to social-auto-upload data but not ctx logs, subject-rights handling becomes inconsistent.
mitigations: Minimize logging of account data.
Set a short log-retention window.
Document deletion/export handling for both agents.
Separate compliance scopes by dataset.
requires-engineering: implement synchronized retention and deletion workflows.
